items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I went down and talked with Mr. Meyers.

ctx.x: In the meantime, there was a program on every Sunday afternoon called the Fitz Bandwagon program. And they would advertise from various cities throughout America, the most popular band in that territory. So we decided to get in the contest. There was a drug company in St. Louis called Meyers Drug Company. They were the key people in the city of St. Louis representing NBC and the agency -- advertising agency who had the account for the Fitz Bandwagon people.

I went down and talked with Mr. Meyers. He was living then. And he told me that all I had to do was get the votes out in different establishments and when they're tallied, the top score would go to the winner. So I got out -- I was married then, and my wife and I, we drove around, over to on Selto and different places in St. Louis, and put these little boxes up, put our names up and asked people to sign our names to it. All over town we did it. Asked the different fellows in the band to do the same thing. Which…
